 FOR SUBSCRIBERS 2026 Election Democrats promised to reverse cuts to Medicaid and food stamps. Trump stands in their way.
 To restore social safety net funding, Democrats will likely need cooperation from the president, who appears to be gearing up for partisan fights. Listen to this article 00:00 00:00  Newly elected Democrats said voters expect action, not excuses, despite the obstacles they face in Washington. Justine Goode / NBC News; Getty Images Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 13, 2026, 6:00 AM EST  /  Updated   Nov. 13, 2026, 8:58 PM EST By Mike Hixenbaugh and Shannon Pettypiece Democrats framed the midterm election as a matter of life and death: Unless they won and reversed Republicans’ historic cuts to healthcare and food assistance, they warned, children would go hungry, rural hospitals would close and Americans would die. Voters handed Democrats their largest midterm popular-vote margin since the Watergate scandal . But what comes next may be harder: delivering on their promises with President Donald Trump still holding the veto pen.
